records.source: וַיְהִ֕י כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר יָשַׁ֥ב דָּוִ֖יד בְּבֵית֑וֹ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜יד אֶל־נָתָ֣ן הַנָּבִ֗יא הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֤י יוֹשֵׁב֙ בְּבֵ֣ית הָֽאֲרָזִ֔ים וַאֲר֥וֹן בְּרִית־יְהוָ֖ה תַּ֥חַת יְרִיעֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And it was when sat David in his house, and said David to Nathan the prophet, See, I [am] dwelling in [the] house of the cedars, and [the] ark of [the] covenant of Yahweh [is] under curtains.
pieces: When David was settled in his house, he said to Nathan the prophet, "Look, I live in a house of cedar, but the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} stays under tent curtains."

L.1: And it happened, when David was dwelling in his house, that David said to Nathan the prophet, "See, I am dwelling in a house of cedar, and the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] under curtains."

R.1: King David was now living in his palace. He said to Nathan the prophet, "Look! I live in a palace made of cedar wood, but the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is kept in a tent."

decisions.choice: his house: his royal palace
decisions.reason: The word means a house, a household or a family. Here it is the palace built for David of cedar sent by Hiram (14:1). The whole chapter turns on this word, as in 2 Samuel 7: David lives in a house (verse 1); he wants to build a house for Yahweh, that is, a temple (verses 4-6, 12); and Yahweh promises instead to build a house for David, a line of kings descended from him (verses 10, 23-25, 27).

decisions.choice: 1 Chronicles 17 retells 2 Samuel 7; here: David, the ark of the covenant, under curtains
decisions.reason: This chapter is the same account as 2 Samuel 7, and most of its words are the same. In this verse it differs in four ways. It names David where Samuel says "the king". It does not have Samuel's words that Yahweh had given him rest from all his enemies; in Chronicles David's wars come after this (chapters 18-20), and rest is promised to Solomon, "a man of rest" (22:9). It says "the ark of the covenant of Yahweh" where Samuel has "the ark of God". And the ark is "under curtains" where Samuel has "inside the curtain", that is, in a tent.

decisions.choice: a house of cedar: a costly royal building
decisions.reason: Cedar was a fine timber brought from Lebanon (14:1; 1 Kings 5:20). A house paneled with it was a mark of royal wealth (Jeremiah 22:14-15).

decisions.choice: curtains: the cloth of a tent
decisions.reason: The word names the cloths of a tent, its curtains or hangings (Exodus 26:1). The ark was kept in the tent David had pitched for it in Jerusalem (15:1; 16:1). The same verb is used for the king living in his house; David does not say what he plans, but the contrast makes it plain, and Nathan understands him (verse 2).

decisions.choice: house (Literal, Balanced); palace (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 7: Literal and Balanced keep the one word "house" all through the chapter so that the reader can follow the play on it (m1). Readable says "palace", "temple" or "family" where the sense is clear, and keeps "house" where the play itself is the point.

decisions.choice: under tent curtains (Balanced); in a tent (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced names the curtains as a tent's; Readable says simply "tent", which is what is meant (m4). Readable also says "King David" and starts a new sentence for his words.

records.heading: God's promise to David

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר נָתָן֙ אֶל־דָּוִ֔יד כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּֽלְבָבְךָ֖ עֲשֵׂ֑ה כִּ֥י הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים עִמָּֽךְ׃ס
records.gloss: And said Nathan to David, All that [is] in your heart do, for the God [is] with you.
pieces: Nathan said to David, "Do all that you have in mind, for God is with you."

L.2: And Nathan said to David, "All that [is] in your heart, do [it], for God [is] with you."

R.2: Nathan answered David, "Do whatever you are planning, because God is with you."

decisions.choice: all that is in your heart: all that you intend
decisions.reason: The heart is where a person thinks and plans, not only where he feels (1 Samuel 14:7).

decisions.choice: Nathan gives his own approval
decisions.reason: Nathan answers from his own judgment, without a word from Yahweh. That same night God speaks to him and turns David's plan another way (verses 3-6). Even a true prophet's own opinion is not the same as God's word.

decisions.choice: to David; do; God is with you
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 7:3 says "to the king", "go, do" and "Yahweh is with you". Chronicles has "to David", only "do", and "God" (literally "the God") in place of the name. Chronicles often says "God" where Samuel has the name Yahweh.

decisions.choice: whatever you are planning
decisions.reason: Readable puts the idiom of the heart in plain words.

records.source: וַֽיְהִ֖י בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַה֑וּא וַיְהִי֙ דְּבַר־אֱלֹהִ֔ים אֶל־נָתָ֖ן לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And it was in the night, that [one], and came [the] word of God to Nathan, saying,
pieces: But that same night the word of God came to Nathan:

L.3: And it happened in that night that the word of God came to Nathan, saying,

R.3: But that very night God gave Nathan a message. God said,

decisions.choice: the word of God came to Nathan: God gave him a message
decisions.reason: This is how the books describe a message given to a prophet (1 Samuel 15:10; 1 Kings 17:2). Verse 15 calls it a vision; it came at night.

decisions.choice: the word of God
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 7:4 has "the word of Yahweh"; Chronicles says "the word of God". The message itself begins "Thus says Yahweh" (verse 4).

decisions.choice: But that same night
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 7:4: the Hebrew joins the verse to what comes before with a plain "and". Balanced and Readable say "But", because God's word overturns Nathan's quick approval.

records.source: לֵ֤ךְ וְאָמַרְתָּ֙ אֶל־דָּוִ֣יד עַבְדִּ֔י כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה לֹ֥א אַתָּ֛ה תִּבְנֶה־לִּ֥י הַבַּ֖יִת לָשָֽׁבֶת׃
records.gloss: Go and you will say to David my servant, Thus says Yahweh, Not you will build for me the house to dwell [in].
pieces: "Go and tell {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: You are not the one who will build {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} the house to live in.

L.4: "Go and say to David {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} slave, 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: You shall not build {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} the house to dwell in.

R.4: "Go and tell {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David, 'This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: You are not the one who will build the house for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to live in.

decisions.choice: my servant David: one who belongs to Yahweh and acts for him
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 7:5. The word is the one used for a slave, a person who belongs to a master. As a title from Yahweh it is an honor, given to Moses (Numbers 12:7) and to Joshua (Joshua 24:29).

decisions.choice: You shall not build: a plain statement, not a question
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 7:5 asks, "Will you build me a house for me to dwell in?", a question that expects the answer no. Chronicles says it outright: "You shall not build me the house to dwell in." It also says "the house", the one David has in mind, and "David my servant" in place of "my servant, David".

decisions.choice: not you: someone else will build it
decisions.reason: The word "you" is stressed. The house will be built, but by David's son (verse 12). 22:8 and 28:3 give the reason: David was a man of war who had shed much blood.

decisions.choice: the house to dwell in
decisions.reason: A temple was thought of as a god's dwelling. Yahweh does not refuse a house (verse 12), but he will not be housed at David's wish; Solomon himself says that the heavens cannot contain him (2 Chronicles 6:18).

decisions.choice: my slave (Literal); my servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 7:5 and the terms used for these books: Literal keeps the hard edge of the word, and Balanced and Readable say "servant", the usual sense of a title of honor (m1).

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD (Literal); The LORD says this (Balanced); This is what the LORD says (Readable)
decisions.reason: The prophet's formula for introducing Yahweh's words keeps one wording at each level in these books.

records.source: כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יָשַׁ֨בְתִּי֙ בְּבַ֔יִת מִן־הַיּ֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֤ר הֶעֱלֵ֨יתִי֙ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה וָֽאֶהְיֶ֛ה מֵאֹ֥הֶל אֶל־אֹ֖הֶל וּמִמִּשְׁכָּֽן׃
records.gloss: For not I have dwelt in a house from the day that I brought up Israel until the day the this, and I have been from tent to tent and from tabernacle.
pieces: I have not lived in a house from the day I brought Israel up until this day. I have moved from one tent to another and from one tabernacle to another.

L.5: For I have not dwelt in a house from the day that I brought up Israel until this day, but I have been from tent to tent and from tabernacle [to tabernacle].

R.5: I have not lived in a house since the day I brought Israel up out of Egypt. All this time I have moved from one tent to another, from one tabernacle to another.

decisions.choice: from tent to tent and from tabernacle [to tabernacle]: from one place to another
alternatives: from tent to tent and from a tabernacle (as the words stand)
decisions.reason: The words are short: "from tent to tent and from tabernacle". The second pair is taken to follow the pattern of the first, so that Yahweh's dwelling moved from place to place. The sanctuary stood at Shiloh (Joshua 18:1) and later at Gibeon (16:39; 21:29), while the ark was kept in other places and at last in a tent in Jerusalem (13:13-14; 16:1).

decisions.choice: I brought up Israel; from tent to tent
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 7:6 says "I brought up the sons of Israel from Egypt" and "I have been going about in a tent and in a tabernacle". Chronicles says "I brought up Israel", without "from Egypt", and "I have been from tent to tent and from tabernacle".

decisions.choice: tent ... tabernacle: the portable sanctuary
decisions.reason: Both words name the sanctuary made in the wilderness: "tent" for its covering and "tabernacle", which means dwelling place, for the place where Yahweh dwelt among his people (Exodus 26:1, 7; 40:34-35).

decisions.choice: [to tabernacle] (Literal); from one tabernacle to another (Balanced)
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the words the short phrase implies (m1); Balanced and Readable say it as one movement from place to place.

decisions.choice: brought Israel up out of Egypt
decisions.reason: Readable says where Yahweh brought Israel up from, as 2 Samuel 7:6 does, and leaves out "until this day", which "all this time" covers.

records.source: בְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶֽׁר־הִתְהַלַּכְתִּי֮ בְּכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ הֲדָבָ֣ר דִּבַּ֗רְתִּי אֶת־אַחַד֙ שֹׁפְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּ֛יתִי לִרְע֥וֹת אֶת־עַמִּ֖י לֵאמֹ֑ר לָ֛מָּה לֹא־בְנִיתֶ֥ם לִ֖י בֵּ֥ית אֲרָזִֽים׃
records.gloss: In all where I have gone about among all Israel, [did] a word I speak with one of [the] judges of Israel whom I commanded to shepherd my people, saying, Why not have you built for me a house of cedars?
pieces: Wherever I have moved about among all Israel, did I ever say a word to any of the judges of Israel that I commanded to shepherd {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, asking, "Why have you not built {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a house of cedar?"'

L.6: In all [places] where I have moved about among all Israel, did I speak a word with one of the judges of Israel, whom I commanded to shepherd {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, saying, "Why have you not built {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a house of cedar?"'

R.6: In all the places I went with the people of Israel, I never said to any of Israel's judges, whom I told to care for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people like a shepherd, "Why have you not built {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a house made of cedar?"'

decisions.choice: judges: the leaders Yahweh appointed
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 7:7 has "one of the tribes of Israel"; Chronicles has "one of the judges of Israel", a word that differs by one letter. "Judges" fits the words that follow, "whom I commanded to shepherd my people", and verse 10 also speaks of judges. Chronicles also says "among all Israel" for "among all the sons of Israel", and "my people" without "Israel".

decisions.choice: to shepherd: to lead and care for
decisions.reason: Shepherding is a common picture of ruling a people: guiding, feeding and protecting them (11:2; Numbers 27:17).

decisions.choice: did I speak a word ...?: I never said this
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer no: Yahweh never asked any of Israel's leaders for a house of cedar.

decisions.choice: judges: Israel's leaders before the kings
decisions.reason: The judges were the leaders Yahweh raised up to rescue Israel from its enemies, from after Joshua to Samuel (Judges 2:16-18; 1 Samuel 7:15).

decisions.choice: I never said to any of Israel's judges
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into the statement it implies, and says "the people of Israel" for "all Israel".

records.source: וְ֠עַתָּה כֹּֽה־תֹאמַ֞ר לְעַבְדִּ֣י לְדָוִ֗ידסכֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת אֲנִ֤י לְקַחְתִּ֨יךָ֙ מִן־הַנָּוֶ֔ה מִֽן־אַחֲרֵ֖י הַצֹּ֑אן לִהְי֣וֹת נָגִ֔יד עַ֖ל עַמִּ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And now thus you will say to my servant, to David, Thus says Yahweh of hosts, I took you from the pasture, from after the flock, to be ruler over my people Israel.
pieces: Now then, say this to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David: '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: I took you from the pasture, from following the sheep, to be ruler over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel.

L.7: And now, thus you shall say to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} slave, to David, 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: I took you from the pasture, from following the flock, to be ruler over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel.

R.7: So now, tell {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David, 'This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: I took you from the fields where you followed the sheep, and I made you leader of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel.

decisions.choice: Yahweh of hosts: Yahweh, commander of armies
decisions.reason: "Hosts" means armies: the armies of Israel and the powers of heaven, all under Yahweh's command (1 Samuel 1:3; 17:45).

decisions.choice: from the pasture, from following the flock
decisions.reason: David was a shepherd boy when Samuel anointed him (1 Samuel 16:11; 17:15, 34). Yahweh took the one who shepherded sheep to shepherd his people (verse 6; 11:2; Psalm 78:70-71). The verse is the same as 2 Samuel 7:8, except that it says "over my people Israel" where Samuel has "over my people, over Israel".

decisions.choice: ruler: the leader Yahweh appoints over his people
decisions.reason: The word names a leader chosen by Yahweh to rule his people for him. It was used of Saul (1 Samuel 9:16; 10:1) and of David (11:2; 1 Samuel 13:14).

decisions.choice: the LORD of hosts (Literal); the LORD of Armies (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in the terms used for these books. "Armies" says in today's English what "hosts" means.

decisions.choice: leader
decisions.reason: Readable says "leader" for the word for ruler, as in the terms used for these books.

records.source: וָֽאֶהְיֶ֣ה עִמְּךָ֗ בְּכֹל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָלַ֔כְתָּ וָאַכְרִ֥ית אֶת־כָּל־אוֹיְבֶ֖יךָ מִפָּנֶ֑יךָ וְעָשִׂ֤יתִֽי לְךָ֙ שֵׁ֔ם כְּשֵׁ֥ם הַגְּדוֹלִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And I have been with you in all where you went, and I cut off all your enemies from before you, and I will make for you a name like [the] name of the great [ones] who [are] on the earth.
pieces: Wherever you have gone, I have been with you, and I have cut off all your enemies in front of you. Now I will make you a name like the names of the greatest people on earth.

L.8: And I have been with you wherever you went, and I have cut off all your enemies from before you, and I will make for you a name like the name of the great ones who [are] on the earth.

R.8: I have been with you everywhere you went. I have destroyed all your enemies as you faced them. Now I will make you famous, like the most famous people in the world.

decisions.choice: I have been, I have cut off ... and I will make: from what Yahweh has done to what he will do
alternatives: I have made for you a name
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 7:9. The first verbs tell what Yahweh has already done for David. With "and I will make" the verb form changes to the one used for the future, and the promises begin. Some read this verb and those in verses 9-10 as still telling the past ("I have made you a name"), but the form and the promise in verse 10 favor the future.

decisions.choice: I will make for you a name
decisions.reason: Yahweh made a like promise to Abram: "I will make your name great" (Genesis 12:2). 2 Samuel 7:9 says "a great name"; Chronicles says "a name like the name of the great ones", with the same sense.

decisions.choice: cut off from before you: destroyed as they faced you
decisions.reason: Yahweh removed David's enemies one by one as David met them in battle (11:4-9; 14:8-17).

decisions.choice: Now
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 7:9: Balanced and Readable add "Now" to mark where the past ends and the promises begin (m1).

decisions.choice: make you famous
decisions.reason: Readable puts "a name" in plain words.

records.source: וְשַׂמְתִּ֣י מָ֠קוֹם לְעַמִּ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל וּנְטַעְתִּ֨יהוּ֙ וְשָׁכַ֣ן תַּחְתָּ֔יו וְלֹ֥א יִרְגַּ֖ז ע֑וֹד וְלֹא־יוֹסִ֤יפוּ בְנֵי־עַוְלָה֙ לְבַלֹּת֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר בָּרִאשׁוֹנָֽה׃
records.gloss: And I will appoint a place for my people Israel, and I will plant it, and it will dwell in its place and not be disturbed again; and not will add sons of injustice to wear it out as at the first,
pieces: I will appoint a place for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel and plant them there, so that they may live in their own place and not be troubled anymore. Wicked people will no longer wear them down as they did at the beginning,

L.9: And I will appoint a place for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel, and I will plant it, and it will dwell in its own place and not be disturbed again; and the sons of wickedness will not again wear it down as at the first,

R.9: I will choose a place for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel. I will plant them there like a tree, so that they can live in their own land and not be afraid anymore. Evil people will not crush them again the way they did before.

decisions.choice: a place: a land where Israel can live in safety
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 7:10. The place is the land where Yahweh will plant his people. The same word is used in Deuteronomy for the place Yahweh will choose for his name (Deuteronomy 12:5), and that may be heard here too; but the words "plant" and "dwell" point to the land.

decisions.choice: I will plant it: settle Israel for good
decisions.reason: Moses' song says Yahweh would plant his people on the mountain of his inheritance (Exodus 15:17; compare Psalm 44:3; 80:9). A planted people is rooted and not moved again.

decisions.choice: sons of wickedness: violent, unjust people
decisions.reason: "Sons of" a quality means people marked by it. Here it means oppressors, like those who afflicted Israel in Egypt and in the time of the judges. The sentence goes on into verse 10: "as at the first, and from the days I appointed judges".

decisions.choice: to wear it down
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 7:10 has "to afflict it"; Chronicles has a verb that means to wear out or use up, as clothing wears out (Deuteronomy 8:4). It also says "for my people Israel" for "for my people, for Israel". The sense is the same: Israel will no longer be worn down by oppressors.

decisions.choice: plant them there like a tree; not be afraid
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 7:10: Readable makes the picture in "plant" plain and says what being "disturbed" means for a people: living in fear. It ends the sentence here, and verse 10 picks it up.

records.source: וּלְמִיָּמִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוִּ֤יתִי שֹֽׁפְטִים֙ עַל־עַמִּ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְהִכְנַ֖עְתִּי אֶת־כָּל־אוֹיְבֶ֑יךָ וָאַגִּ֣ד לָ֔ךְ וּבַ֖יִת יִֽבְנֶה־לְּךָ֥ יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: and from [the] days that I appointed judges over my people Israel. And I will subdue all your enemies. And I declare to you that a house will build for you Yahweh.
pieces: ever since the time I set judges over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel. I will also bring all your enemies low. And I declare to you that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will build you a house.

L.10: and from the days that I appointed judges over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel. And I will subdue all your enemies. And I declare to you that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will build a house for you.

R.10: They did that from the time I put judges over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel. And I will defeat all your enemies. I tell you now that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will build a house for you, a family of kings who will come after you.

decisions.choice: a house: a family line of kings
decisions.reason: Here the play on the word turns. David wanted to build God a house of cedar; Yahweh will build David a house of a different kind, a family of descendants who will sit on his throne (verses 11-14). Chronicles uses the verb "build" here, where 2 Samuel 7:11 has "make": the house David will not build for Yahweh (verse 4), Yahweh builds for him.

decisions.choice: I will subdue all your enemies; I declare to you; build
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 7:11 says "I will give you rest from all your enemies"; Chronicles says "I will subdue all your enemies". In Chronicles David's victories follow at once (18:1, where the same verb is used of the Philistines), and the rest is kept for Solomon (22:9). Samuel then has "Yahweh declares to you that Yahweh will make a house for you"; Chronicles has "I declare to you that Yahweh will build a house for you". It also has "from the days" for "from the day".

decisions.choice: subdue: humble, bring low
decisions.reason: The verb means to bring an enemy down so that he submits (Judges 4:23; 1 Samuel 7:13).

decisions.choice: I declare to you: the announcement is made now
decisions.reason: The verb form usually tells something past, "and I told you". Here it is taken as the solemn announcement Yahweh makes in this very message. Some read it "I have told you", looking back to earlier promises to David.

decisions.choice: a house, a family of kings who will come after you
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 7:11: Readable keeps the word "house" for the play on it and adds what it means here (m1). It also starts a new sentence that links back to the oppression of verse 9.

decisions.choice: bring low (Balanced); defeat (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "bring low", what the verb pictures (m3), and Readable says "defeat", for the less common "subdue".

records.source: וְהָיָ֗ה כִּֽי־מָלְא֤וּ יָמֶ֨יךָ֙ לָלֶ֣כֶת עִם־אֲבֹתֶ֔יךָ וַהֲקִֽימוֹתִ֤י אֶֽת־זַרְעֲךָ֙ אַחֲרֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִהְיֶ֖ה מִבָּנֶ֑יךָ וַהֲכִינוֹתִ֖י אֶת־מַלְכוּתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And it will be, when are fulfilled your days to go with your fathers, and I will raise up your seed after you, who will be from your sons, and I will establish his kingdom.
pieces: When your days are complete and you go to be with your ancestors, I will raise up your offspring after you, one of your own sons, and I will make his kingdom firm.

L.11: And it will be, when your days are fulfilled to go [to be] with your fathers, that I will raise up your offspring after you, who will be one of your sons, and I will establish his kingdom.

R.11: When your life is over and you die, I will make one of your own sons king after you. I will make his kingdom strong.

decisions.choice: your days are fulfilled to go with your fathers: you die
decisions.reason: To go to one's fathers is a way of speaking of death (Genesis 15:15). 2 Samuel 7:12 has "you lie down with your fathers", the usual phrase in these books.

decisions.choice: your offspring: first one son, and through him a line
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 7:12. The word means seed, and so offspring. It can mean one descendant or a whole line of them. Here it is first one son, who will build the house (verse 12): Solomon, as David himself says (22:9-10; 28:5-6). But the promise reaches on to the whole line that follows (verse 14).

decisions.choice: who will be one of your sons
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 7:12 says "who will come out from your body", the words of Yahweh's promise to Abram (Genesis 15:4). Chronicles says "who will be from your sons": one of the sons David already has, whose names it has listed (3:1-9; 14:3-7).

decisions.choice: I will raise up: bring forward and set in place
decisions.reason: The verb is used for Yahweh setting a leader in place for his people (Judges 2:16; 1 Samuel 2:35).

decisions.choice: go to be with your ancestors
decisions.reason: Balanced says "ancestors" for "fathers", as in the wording kept for the death formula; Readable says simply "die".

decisions.choice: I will make one of your own sons king after you
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 7:12: Readable names what the offspring is in this verse, a son, and what being raised up means for him, becoming king.

records.source: ה֥וּא יִבְנֶה־לִּ֖י בָּ֑יִת וְכֹנַנְתִּ֥י אֶת־כִּסְא֖וֹ עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: He will build for me a house, and I will establish his throne until forever.
pieces: He is the one who will build {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a house, and I will make his throne firm forever.

L.12: He will build {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a house, and I will establish his throne forever.

R.12: He is the one who will build a house for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, a temple. And I will make sure that his throne will last forever.

decisions.choice: he will build: he, not you
decisions.reason: The word "he" is stressed, answering verse 4: David will not build the house, but his son will (22:9-10; 28:6).

decisions.choice: a house for me; his throne
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 7:13 says "a house for my name" and "the throne of his kingdom". Chronicles says "a house for me" and "his throne". The sense is the same: the temple is Yahweh's house, and the son's throne will stand.

decisions.choice: forever: for all time to come
decisions.reason: The phrase looks to a time without a set end. The word comes again and again in the chapter (verses 14, 22, 23, 24, 27). When the line of kings was broken at the exile, the prophets and psalms held to this promise (Psalm 89:30, 37-38; Jeremiah 33:17), and the New Testament sees it kept in Jesus, the son of David (Luke 1:32-33).

decisions.choice: a house, a temple
decisions.reason: Readable says that this house is a temple, keeping the word "house" for the play on it.

records.source: אֲנִי֙ אֶֽהְיֶה־לּ֣וֹ לְאָ֔ב וְה֖וּא יִֽהְיֶה־לִּ֣י לְבֵ֑ן וְחַסְדִּי֙ לֹא־אָסִ֣יר מֵֽעִמּ֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר הֲסִיר֔וֹתִי מֵאֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיָ֖ה לְפָנֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: I will be to him for a father, and he will be to me for a son; and my steadfast love not I will remove from with him, as I removed [it] from [the one] who was before you.
pieces: I will be a father to him, and he will be a son to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I will not take {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} faithful love away from him, as I took it away from the one who was before you.

L.13: I will be to him a father, and he will be to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a son; and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} steadfast love I will not remove from him, as I removed [it] from the one who was before you.

R.13: I will be his father, and he will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} son. And {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} faithful love will stay with him. I will never take it away, the way I took it from the king who ruled before you.

decisions.choice: I will be his father, and he will be my son: a bond of covenant care and loyalty
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 7:14. Yahweh takes David's son into a relation like that of father and son: Yahweh will care for him and guide him, and the king is to honor and obey him and rule for him. David repeats the words of Solomon (22:10; 28:6), and the psalms use them of the king of David's line (Psalm 2:7; 89:27-28).

decisions.choice: Hebrews 1:5 quotes these words of the Son
decisions.reason: Hebrews 1:5 quotes the first half of this verse (with 2 Samuel 7:14 and Psalm 2:7) as words spoken of Jesus as the Son. In their first setting they are said of the son of David who will build the temple. Hebrews reads the promise to David's line as finding its fullest meaning in Jesus, the descendant of David.

decisions.choice: no words about wrongdoing; I will not remove; the one who was before you
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 7:14-15 goes on: "When he does wrong, I will correct him with the rod of men". Chronicles does not have these words, and moves straight to the promise of faithful love. It says "I will not remove my love from him" where Samuel has "my love will not depart from him", and "the one who was before you" where Samuel names Saul.

decisions.choice: my steadfast love: Yahweh's loyal, faithful love
decisions.reason: The word names love that keeps faith with a bond: kindness that does not let go (1 Samuel 20:14-15). Here Yahweh binds himself to David's son without condition. Isaiah 55:3 calls it "the faithful love promised to David".

decisions.choice: the one who was before you: Saul
decisions.reason: Saul ruled before David, and Yahweh took the kingdom from him and turned it over to David (10:13-14).

decisions.choice: steadfast love (Literal); faithful love (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in the terms used for these books and in Exodus 34:6.

decisions.choice: the king who ruled before you
decisions.reason: Readable says that the one before David was a king (m5).

records.source: וְהַֽעֲמַדְתִּ֛יהוּ בְּבֵיתִ֥י וּבְמַלְכוּתִ֖י עַד־הָעוֹלָ֑ם וְכִסְא֕וֹ יִהְיֶ֥ה נָכ֖וֹן עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: And I will cause him to stand in my house and in my kingdom until forever, and his throne will be established until forever.
pieces: I will keep him in place over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} kingdom forever, and his throne will stand firm for all time.'"

L.14: And I will set him in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house and in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} kingdom forever, and his throne will be established forever.'"

R.14: I will put him in charge of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} kingdom forever. His throne will last forever.'"

decisions.choice: my house and my kingdom: the kingdom is Yahweh's
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 7:16 says "your house and your kingdom will be made sure forever before you". Chronicles says "I will set him in my house and in my kingdom". The kingdom belongs to Yahweh, and the son of David rules it for him; Chronicles says this again and again (28:5; 29:23; 2 Chronicles 9:8; 13:8).

decisions.choice: my house: Yahweh's household, his people and his temple
decisions.reason: "My house" can mean the temple the son will build (verse 12), or Yahweh's household, the people he rules. Set beside "my kingdom", it most likely means the second, without excluding the first.

decisions.choice: I will set him: appoint him and keep him in place
decisions.reason: The verb means to make someone stand, and so to appoint and confirm him in a position (2 Chronicles 9:8).

decisions.choice: his throne established forever: an unconditional promise
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 7:16, the line and throne will remain. Later passages keep this hope alive after the kings had fallen (Psalm 89:30-38; Amos 9:11; Isaiah 9:6), and the New Testament announces Jesus as the one who receives David's throne forever (Luke 1:32-33).

decisions.choice: over my house (Balanced); in charge of my house (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "in". Balanced and Readable say what being set "in" a house and kingdom means here: to be set over them as ruler.

records.source: כְּכֹל֙ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה וּכְכֹ֖ל הֶחָז֣וֹן הַזֶּ֑ה כֵּ֛ן דִּבֶּ֥ר נָתָ֖ן אֶל־דָּוִֽיד׃פ
records.gloss: According to all the words the these and according to all the vision the this, so spoke Nathan to David.
pieces: Nathan spoke to David in keeping with all these words and all this vision.

L.15: According to all these words and according to all this vision, so Nathan spoke to David.

R.15: Nathan told David everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said to him in this vision.

decisions.choice: vision: a revelation given by God
decisions.reason: The word names a message seen or received from God. This one came at night (verse 3).

decisions.choice: so Nathan spoke: he passed on all of it
decisions.reason: Nathan told David everything, though it overturned his own word of approval (verse 2). The verse is the same as 2 Samuel 7:17.

decisions.choice: everything the LORD had said to him
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 7:17: Readable names the speaker behind "these words" (verse 4).

records.source: וַיָּבֹא֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֔יד וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר מִֽי־אֲנִ֞י יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהִים֙ וּמִ֣י בֵיתִ֔י כִּ֥י הֲבִיאֹתַ֖נִי עַד־הֲלֹֽם׃
records.gloss: And went King David and sat before Yahweh and said, Who [am] I, Yahweh God, and who [is] my house, that you have brought me as far as here?
pieces: Then King David went in and sat down before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and said, "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} God, who am I, and what is my house, that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have brought me as far as this?

L.16: And King David went in and sat before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and said, "Who [am] I, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} God, and what [is] my house, that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have brought me this far?

R.16: Then King David went into the tent and sat down in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He said, "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} God, who am I? And what is my family? Why have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} brought me this far?

decisions.choice: sat before Yahweh: in the tent where the ark was kept
decisions.reason: To be "before Yahweh" was to be in his presence at the sanctuary, here the tent David had set up for the ark in Jerusalem (16:1; verse 1). Sitting to pray is unusual; David sits as one at home in Yahweh's presence.

decisions.choice: Yahweh God: not "my Lord Yahweh"
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 7:18-29 addresses Yahweh again and again as "my Lord Yahweh". Chronicles never uses that title here: it has "Yahweh God" (verses 16, 17), "God" (verse 17), "my God" (verse 25) or the name Yahweh alone (verses 19, 20, 22, 23, 26, 27). Otherwise this verse is the same as 2 Samuel 7:18.

decisions.choice: Who am I ...?: I am not worthy of this
decisions.reason: The question is a way of saying how small one is before a great gift or task (1 Samuel 18:18; Exodus 3:11).

decisions.choice: my house: my family
decisions.reason: Here David's house is his family, not the palace. He has just heard that Yahweh will build it into a house of kings (verse 10).

decisions.choice: LORD God (when David speaks to him)
decisions.reason: When the divine name is used to address Yahweh it is printed "LORD" without "the", as in 2 Samuel 7:24-25.

decisions.choice: went into the tent
decisions.reason: Readable says where David went (m1).

records.heading: David's prayer

records.source: וַתִּקְטַ֨ן זֹ֤את בְּעֵינֶ֨יךָ֙ אֱלֹהִ֔ים וַתְּדַבֵּ֥ר עַל־בֵּֽית־עַבְדְּךָ֖ לְמֵרָח֑וֹק וּרְאִיתַ֗נִי כְּת֧וֹר הָאָדָ֛ם הַֽמַּעֲלָ֖ה יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: And was small this in your eyes, O God, and you have spoken about [the] house of your servant for from far; and you have seen me according to [the] rank of the man of the ascent, Yahweh God.
pieces: And as if this were too little in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sight, God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have also spoken about the house of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant far into the future. You have regarded me as a man of high rank, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} God.

L.17: And this was small in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} eyes, God, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have spoken of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant's house for a distant [time], and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have regarded me according to the rank of a man of high degree, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} God.

R.17: And as if that were not enough, God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have also made promises about my family for a long time to come. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have treated me as if I were a man of great importance.

decisions.choice: this was small in your eyes: as if this were not enough for you
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 7:19. What God has done for David already is great, yet to God it was a small thing, and he has added more.

decisions.choice: for a distant time: far into the future
decisions.reason: "From far" can speak of distance in space or time. Here it is the future: God has spoken of David's house in the generations to come.

decisions.choice: you have regarded me according to the rank of a man of high degree: you have treated me as a great man
alternatives: you have shown me the future generations of humankind
and this is the custom of humankind (2 Samuel 7:19)
decisions.reason: The words are hard to understand, and they differ from 2 Samuel 7:19, which has "and this is the law (or custom) of humankind". Word for word they say "you have seen me according to the turn (or order) of the man of the going up". The translation takes "order" as rank and "going up" as high standing: God has looked on David as one of the great. Others take the words as "you have shown me the generations of humankind to come", reading "going up" as onward in time and "seen me" as "made me see". The Hebrew may have suffered in copying, and no reading is certain.

decisions.choice: God; Yahweh God
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 7:19 has "my Lord Yahweh" twice; Chronicles has "God" and "Yahweh God" (verse 16).

decisions.choice: your servant: David himself
decisions.reason: Calling oneself "your servant" is a polite and humble way of saying "I" when speaking to a superior (1 Samuel 17:32). David uses it again and again in this prayer.

decisions.choice: your servant (Literal, Balanced); my family (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 7:19: "your servant" stays at every level as the polite form of address, and Readable often says "I", "me" or "my" instead, since the phrase is a polite way of saying "I".

decisions.choice: treated me as if I were a man of great importance
decisions.reason: Readable puts the reading taken in m3 in plain words; it carries the same uncertainty.

records.source: מַה־יּוֹסִ֨יף ע֥וֹד דָּוִ֛יד אֵלֶ֖יךָ לְכָב֣וֹד אֶת־עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ וְאַתָּ֖ה אֶֽת־עַבְדְּךָ֥ יָדָֽעְתָּ׃
records.gloss: What will add again David to you for [the] honor of your servant? And you, your servant you know.
pieces: What more can David say to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} about the honor {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have shown {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant? You know {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant.

L.18: What more can David add to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} for the honor of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant? For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} know {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant.

R.18: What more can I say to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} about the way {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have honored me? You know {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant.

decisions.choice: What more can David add?: David speaks of himself by name
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 7:20. David names himself, as a servant might before his master. The question means he has nothing to add: God's gift goes beyond words.

decisions.choice: for the honor of your servant: the honor God has given David
decisions.reason: The honor is what God has done for David in the promise; David can add nothing to it.

decisions.choice: add ... for the honor of your servant
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 7:20 says "What more can David add to speak to you?" and ends with "my Lord Yahweh". Chronicles says "What more can David add to you for the honor of your servant?" and has no title at the end.

decisions.choice: you know your servant: you know me through and through
decisions.reason: To know a person can mean more than to be aware of him: to know him closely and to have chosen him (Genesis 18:19; Amos 3:2).

decisions.choice: say ... about the honor you have shown
decisions.reason: Balanced says what "add" means here, adding words, and whose honor it is.

decisions.choice: I
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 7:20: Readable says "I" for David's name, which in English would sound as if someone else were meant, and keeps "your servant" at the end.

records.source: יְהוָ֕ה בַּעֲב֤וּר עַבְדְּךָ֙ וּֽכְלִבְּךָ֔ עָשִׂ֕יתָ אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַגְּדוּלָּ֖ה הַזֹּ֑את לְהֹדִ֖יעַ אֶת־כָּל־הַגְּדֻלּֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: Yahweh, for [the] sake of your servant and according to your heart you have done all the greatness the this, to make known all the great [things].
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant and as {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own heart chose, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done this great thing, to make all these great things known.

L.19: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant and according to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} heart {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done all this greatness, to make known all the great [things].

R.19: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done this great thing for my sake and because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} wanted to. You have made all these great things known.

decisions.choice: for your servant's sake; to make known all the great things
alternatives: for the sake of your word (2 Samuel 7:21)
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 7:21 has "for the sake of your word" and "to make it known to your servant". Chronicles has "for the sake of your servant" and "to make known all the great things", and it begins with the name, "Yahweh".

decisions.choice: according to your heart: as you yourself chose
decisions.reason: What Yahweh has done comes from his own will, not from anything David earned (compare 1 Samuel 13:14).

decisions.choice: this greatness ... the great things: great deeds
decisions.reason: The word means greatness, and here a great thing done: the promise of a lasting house. Its plural, "great things", is all that Yahweh has promised and made known.

decisions.choice: for my sake
decisions.reason: Readable says "my" for "your servant" (verse 17).

decisions.choice: LORD (when David speaks to him)
decisions.reason: As in verse 16.

records.source: יְהוָה֙ אֵ֣ין כָּמ֔וֹךָ וְאֵ֥ין אֱלֹהִ֖ים זוּלָתֶ֑ךָ בְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־שָׁמַ֖עְנוּ בְּאָזְנֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: Yahweh, there is none like you, and there is no God except you, in all that we have heard with our ears.
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, there is no one like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and there is no God but {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, as all we have heard with our own ears tells us.

L.20: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, there is none like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and there is no God besides {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, according to all that we have heard with our ears.

R.20: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, no one is like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. There is no God except {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. Everything we have ever heard tells us so.

decisions.choice: there is none like you, and no God except you
decisions.reason: David uses the words of Israel's basic confession (Deuteronomy 4:35, 39) and of Hannah's prayer (1 Samuel 2:2).

decisions.choice: Yahweh, there is none like you
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 7:22 begins "Therefore you are great, my Lord Yahweh, for there is none like you". Chronicles begins simply "Yahweh" and goes straight to "there is none like you".

decisions.choice: all that we have heard with our ears: what has been told from generation to generation
decisions.reason: Israel knew Yahweh's deeds from what parents told their children (Psalm 44:2; Judges 6:13).

decisions.choice: LORD (when David speaks to him)
decisions.reason: As in verse 16.

records.source: וּמִי֙ כְּעַמְּךָ֣ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל גּ֥וֹי אֶחָ֖ד בָּאָ֑רֶץ אֲשֶׁר֩ הָלַ֨ךְ הָאֱלֹהִ֜ים לִפְדּ֧וֹת ל֣וֹ עָ֗ם לָשׂ֤וּם לְךָ֙ שֵׁ֚ם גְּדֻלּ֣וֹת וְנֹרָא֔וֹת לְגָרֵ֗שׁ מִפְּנֵ֧י עַמְּךָ֛ אֲשֶׁר־פָּדִ֥יתָ מִמִּצְרַ֖יִם גּוֹיִֽם׃
records.gloss: And who [is] like your people Israel, one nation on the earth, whom went the God to redeem for himself [as] a people, to make for you a name [of] great [things] and awesome [things], by driving out from before your people, whom you redeemed from Egypt, nations?
pieces: Who is there like {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people Israel, the one nation on earth that God went to redeem as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own people? You made a name for {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} by great and awesome deeds, driving out nations before {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} redeemed from Egypt.

L.21: And who [is] like {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people Israel, one nation on the earth, whom God went to redeem for {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} as a people, to make for {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} a name [by] great and awesome [things], by driving out nations from before {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} redeemed from Egypt?

R.21: There is no nation on earth like {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people Israel! God went to set them free so that they would be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own people. You made {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name famous by doing great and amazing things. You drove out other nations to make room for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} set free from Egypt.

decisions.choice: who is like your people ...?: Israel's unique story
decisions.reason: David echoes Moses: no other god ever went to take a nation for himself out of another nation, with signs and wonders, as Yahweh did for Israel in Egypt (Deuteronomy 4:7, 32-34; 33:29).

decisions.choice: redeem: set free from slavery
decisions.reason: The verb means to free someone by paying a price. It is used of Yahweh rescuing Israel from slavery in Egypt (Deuteronomy 7:8; 9:26).

decisions.choice: for himself ... for yourself: David turns from speaking of God to speaking to him
decisions.reason: David speaks of God in the third person ("God went to redeem for himself") and then turns to address him ("to make for yourself a name").

decisions.choice: driving out nations: the differences from 2 Samuel 7:23
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 7:23 is hard to read as it stands: it has a plural verb, "God (or gods) went", and "to do for you greatness and awesome things for your land, before your people ... nations and its gods". Chronicles has the singular verb, "for yourself a name", and "by driving out nations from before your people". It has no "for your land" and no "gods", and "whom you redeemed from Egypt" without "for yourself".

decisions.choice: [by] great and awesome [things]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the words that join "a name" to the great deeds that made it.

decisions.choice: the question broken into shorter sentences
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable break the long question into shorter sentences, and Readable turns the question into the statement it implies.

pieces: You made {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people Israel {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own people forever, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, have become their God.

L.22: And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people Israel a people for {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} forever, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, have become their God.

R.22: You made Israel {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own people forever. And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, became their God.

decisions.choice: your people ... you have become their God: the covenant
decisions.reason: This is the covenant promise: "I will take you as my people, and I will be your God" (Exodus 6:7; Leviticus 26:12; Deuteronomy 29:12).

decisions.choice: you made
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 7:24 has "you established", the verb used for David's kingdom and throne. Chronicles has "you made" (literally "you gave" or "set"). Otherwise the verse is the same.

decisions.choice: LORD (when David speaks to him)
decisions.reason: As in verse 16.

records.gloss: And now, Yahweh, the word that you have spoken about your servant and about his house, let be confirmed until forever, and do as you have spoken.
pieces: And now, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, let the word {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have spoken about {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant and about his house stand firm forever, and do as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have said.

L.23: And now, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, let the word that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have spoken concerning {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant and concerning his house be confirmed forever, and do as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have spoken.

R.23: So now, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, please keep forever the promise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made about me, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, and about my family. Do what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} said.

decisions.choice: let it be confirmed: let it prove true and stand firm
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the root that gives "amen" and "faithful": something that can be relied on to stand. David repeats it at the start of verse 24.

decisions.choice: do as you have spoken: prayer that holds Yahweh to his promise
decisions.reason: David asks only for what Yahweh has already promised. His prayer rests on Yahweh's word, not on his own wishes.

decisions.choice: Yahweh; let it be confirmed
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 7:25 has "Yahweh God" and "confirm it" (literally "make it stand"), asking Yahweh to act. Chronicles has "Yahweh" and "let it be confirmed", a verb from the root of "amen".

decisions.choice: the promise
decisions.reason: Readable says what the word here is: a promise.

decisions.choice: your servant (Literal, Balanced); me, your servant (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 17.

records.gloss: And let it be confirmed, and let be great your name until forever, saying, Yahweh of hosts, God of Israel, [is] God to Israel; and [the] house of David your servant [is] established before you.
pieces: Let it stand firm, and may {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name be great forever, as people say, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, is Israel's God!' And the house of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant David will stand firm before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

L.24: And let it be confirmed, and may {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name be great forever, saying, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, the God of Israel, [is] God to Israel'; and the house of David {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant [will be] established before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

R.24: Let it come true, so that people will honor {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name forever. They will say, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, truly is Israel's God!' And my family, the family of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant David, will stand firm in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} presence.

decisions.choice: let it be confirmed, and may your name be great: a wish, with its result
decisions.reason: The verbs express a wish. When Yahweh keeps his word, his name will be honored and people will say who he is.

decisions.choice: the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, is Israel's God
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 7:26 has "Yahweh of hosts is God over Israel". Chronicles has "Yahweh of hosts, the God of Israel, is God to Israel": the name people call him by will be proved true in what he does for Israel. Chronicles also begins with "let it be confirmed", repeating verse 23, and says "the house of David your servant".

decisions.choice: established: made firm
decisions.reason: The same word as in verse 14. David's house stands firm "before" Yahweh, in his presence and under his care.

decisions.choice: the LORD of hosts (Literal); the LORD of Armies (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 7.

decisions.choice: truly is Israel's God
decisions.reason: Readable adds "truly" to bring out that the title will be shown to be true (m2).

decisions.choice: your servant (every level); my family (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 17.

records.gloss: For you, my God, have uncovered [the] ear of your servant, to build for him a house; therefore has found your servant to pray before you.
pieces: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, my God, have made it known to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will build him a house. That is why {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant has found the courage to pray before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

L.25: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, my God, have uncovered the ear of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, to build him a house; therefore {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant has found [courage] to pray before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

R.25: My God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have told me, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will build a house for me, a family of kings. That is why I have been bold enough to pray to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: uncovered the ear: revealed
decisions.reason: To uncover someone's ear is to tell him something he did not know (1 Samuel 9:15; 20:2).

decisions.choice: my God; to build him a house; found to pray
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 7:27 has "Yahweh of hosts, God of Israel", quotes Yahweh's words "I will build a house for you", and says that David "has found his heart to pray this prayer to you". Chronicles has "my God", reports the promise ("to build him a house"), and says only that David "has found to pray before you".

decisions.choice: has found [courage]: found the boldness to pray
decisions.reason: The verb "found" has no object here. 2 Samuel 7:27 has "found his heart", that is, found courage, and that is the sense here: Yahweh's promise has given David the boldness to ask.

decisions.choice: [courage] (Literal); the courage (Balanced)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced supply what David found (m3); Readable says "bold enough".

decisions.choice: a house, a family of kings
decisions.reason: As in verse 10, Readable adds what the house is, and says "me" and "I" for "your servant" and "him".

records.gloss: And now, Yahweh, you, he [is] the God, and you have spoken about your servant the good [thing] the this.
pieces: And now, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are God, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have promised this good thing to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant.

L.26: And now, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are God, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have spoken this good [thing] to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant.

R.26: Now, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} alone are God. You have promised this good thing to me, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant.

decisions.choice: you are God: you and no other
decisions.reason: The words, literally "you, he is the God", stress that Yahweh is the one true God (Deuteronomy 4:35; 1 Kings 18:39).

decisions.choice: this good thing: the promised blessing
decisions.reason: "Good" here is the good that Yahweh has promised: the lasting house (compare 1 Samuel 25:30).

decisions.choice: Yahweh; no "your words are truth"
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 7:28 has "my Lord Yahweh" and adds "and your words are truth". Chronicles has "Yahweh" and does not have those words.

decisions.choice: LORD (when David speaks to him)
decisions.reason: As in verse 16.

decisions.choice: your servant (every level); me (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 17.

records.gloss: And now you have been willing to bless [the] house of your servant to be forever before you; for you, Yahweh, have blessed, and [it is] blessed forever.
pieces: So now it has pleased {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to bless the house of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, so that it may last before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} forever. For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, have blessed it, and it is blessed forever."

L.27: And now {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have been pleased to bless the house of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, so that it may be forever before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, have blessed [it], and [it is] blessed forever."

R.27: Now {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have chosen to bless my family, so that it will last forever in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} presence. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have blessed it, and so it will be blessed forever."

decisions.choice: you have been pleased; you have blessed, and it is blessed
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 7:29 asks, "be pleased to bless", and ends "for you, my Lord Yahweh, have spoken, and with your blessing the house of your servant will be blessed forever". Chronicles says "you have been pleased to bless", speaking of the blessing as already given, and ends "for you, Yahweh, have blessed, and it is blessed forever".

decisions.choice: be pleased: be willing, agree
decisions.reason: The verb means to be willing or to agree to do something. David speaks of Yahweh's willingness as already shown in his promise.

decisions.choice: bless ... blessed ... blessed: the prayer ends in confidence
decisions.reason: The word for blessing comes three times, and the prayer closes, like Nathan's message (verse 14), on David's house lasting forever. What Yahweh has blessed stays blessed.

decisions.choice: LORD (when David speaks to him)
decisions.reason: As in verse 16.

decisions.choice: your servant (Literal, Balanced); my family (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 17: Readable says "my family" for "the house of your servant".
